items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: My band and Ken's were engaged to do a radio show which also included an Austrian tenor sax player named Hans Kohler

ctx.x: The waitresses were mostly not younger than 40 years, dressed in typical German costumes and they could serve from ten to twelve big mugs of beer by carrying them in their hands and not using trays. The orchestra was Tyrolian and consisted of about 18 people including singers. They had a game which was to invite someone on the bandstand to direct the orchestra which was fun. And when the person who directed the orchestra was finished at the end of the number, be it man or woman, they had to pay a round of beer or…

There was an English orchestra under the leadership of a trumpet player named Ken Coller and his brother Bill, who was playing at a club near the Ripperbahn. My band and Ken's were engaged to do a radio show which also included an Austrian tenor sax player named Hans Kohler, who was very popular in Germany. Ken played the real old time New Orleans jazz and most of the numbers he played on the show were things that I had never heard played by some of the New Orleans orchestras back home. I remember that they were…

Hans had his trio and his style was a little like Lester Young and Stan Getz. For a musical variety show, this set up was alright because there was the old style New Orleans music of Ken Colyer, the more modern Middle jazz style of me and my band, and the modern style of the 1950's played by Hans Kohler.
